transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because for the last couple years I’ve just felt low pretty much all the time. Even when I’m at work, or at church, or around people I care about, there’s this heavy, empty feeling that doesn’t really go away.
Have you ever had any periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or so good that others noticed you were different?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember a time where I felt unusually high or full of energy like that, or where other people said I was acting different in that way.
Before these feelings started, did you experience any major life changes, losses, or stressful events that you feel might be connected to how you’ve been feeling?

Yeah. It started after I had to stop taking my community college classes. I couldn’t keep up with the cost and my work schedule, so I just had to quit. That was about two years and four months ago, and since then things have felt this way.
Have you noticed your mood improving at all, even temporarily, during positive events or when spending time with people you care about?

Not really. Even when something good happens, or I’m with people I care about, it might distract me for a little bit, but the low feeling is still there. It just feels heavy and empty most of the time, like it doesn’t really lift.
Have there been any periods during these last two years when you felt significantly better for a few days or weeks, or has the low feeling been pretty much constant the whole time?

It’s been pretty much constant. I mean, I might get distracted for a little while if I’m at work or church or around people I care about, but that heavy, empty feeling is still there. I don’t really remember a stretch of days or weeks where I felt significantly better.
So you mentioned the low feeling has been there for about two years now — has there ever been even a single day or two during this time where you felt completely free of this low mood, even briefly?

No, I don’t think so. Even on days where I’m busy at work or at church, or with people I care about, it’s still kind of there underneath. I can get distracted for a bit, but I don’t feel like it ever fully goes away.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight, trouble sleeping or sleeping too much, or difficulty concentrating on tasks during this time?

Yeah, my appetite’s been off. A lot of days I don’t really eat during my shift because nothing sounds good, and then later I’ll just grab something from the vending machine because I’m exhausted. My weight kind of goes up and down too — enough that my work pants fit different some months.
Have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to enjoy, or that activities you used to find meaningful or fun just don’t seem to matter anymore?

Yeah. I’ve mostly stopped doing the things I used to actually care about. I used to go to basketball and dance nights, and I was helping with the church STEM mentoring, but I barely show up anymore. Even work has been affected — I’ve gotten written warnings because I’ve missed shifts and turned in my inspection paperwork late. It’s like I know those things mattered to me, but I just can’t make myself care or keep up.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving more slowly than usual, or that you can’t seem to sit still and feel restless?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower or being especially restless. I mean, I feel worn down a lot, but I can’t say I’ve clearly seen that in how I move.
Would you say that your mood has been consistently low every day, nearly all day, for at least two years?

Yeah… I would say so. For the last couple years I’ve felt low most of the time, pretty much every day. Even when I’m at work or at church or around people I care about, there’s still this heavy, empty feeling that doesn’t really go away.
Have you noticed feeling significantly fatigued or having a loss of energy during this time, even when you haven’t been physically active?

Yes. I feel tired even when I haven’t really done anything. Small things like filling out the inspection logs, driving to basketball, or even washing my hair feel like they take more energy than I have. And resting on my days off doesn’t really make me feel recharged.
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling worthless or guilty about things more often during this time?
I’m not really sure. I do feel bad about myself sometimes, but I can’t say I’ve noticed a clear pattern of feeling worthless or guilty more often.

Have there been any days in the past two years where your mood felt even worse than usual, or where you completely lost interest in everything, even more than the general low feeling you've described?

Yeah… there have been days where it feels heavier than usual, but honestly the main thing is that it’s kind of always there. For the last couple years I’ve just felt low most of the time, like even at work or church or when I’m with people I care about, that empty feeling doesn’t really lift.
